description: In the 31st Chaupai, Mother Sita blesses Hanuman with the ability to grant the *Ashta-Siddhi* (the eight supernatural Yogic powers). A master of these Siddhis can manipulate the fundamental building blocks of matter and space.

items.name: **Anima**
items.description: The power to shrink one's body to the size of an atom or sub-atomic particle (used to secretly enter Lanka).

items.name: **Mahima**
items.description: The power to expand one's body to an infinitely large, gargantuan size (used to terrify the demoness Surasa).

items.name: **Garima**
items.description: The power to become infinitely heavy (used when Bhima could not lift even Hanuman's tail).

items.name: **Laghima**
items.description: The power to become almost weightless or lighter than air (used for levitation and swift flight across the ocean).

items.name: **Prapti**
items.description: The power to instantly acquire or reach anything anywhere, regardless of physical barriers.

items.name: **Prakamya**
items.description: The power to realize any desire, achieve irresistible willpower, and instantly materialize objects.

items.name: **Ishitva**
items.description: The power of absolute lordship and supreme dominance over nature and living beings.

items.name: **Vashitva**
items.description: The ultimate power to conquer, subjugate, or mesmerize any entity to follow one's will.

description: Alongside the 8 Siddhis, Sita also granted Hanuman dominion over the *Nava-Nidhi* (the nine divine, inexhaustible treasures of Kubera, the god of wealth). These are not merely financial riches, but profound spiritual and cosmic abundances.

items.name: **Mahapadma**
items.description: The ''Great Lotus Casket'' containing immense wealth, generating generations of prosperity and philanthropy.

items.name: **Padma**
items.description: The ''Lotus Casket'' offering abundant material riches, sattvic tendencies, and untainted gifts.

items.name: **Shankha**
items.description: The ''Conch Shell'' bringing self-sustaining wealth, typically enjoyed and isolated by the owner.

items.name: **Makara**
items.description: The ''Crocodile'' granting martial proficiency, strategic intellect, and dominance in warfare/arms.

items.name: **Kacchapa**
items.description: The ''Tortoise'' establishing wealth accumulated slowly, hidden secretly, and passed down carefully.

items.name: **Mukunda**
items.description: The ''Quicksilver'' or ''Kettle'' bringing an aesthetic inclination towards fine arts, music, and royal patronage.

items.name: **Kunda**
items.description: The ''Jasmine'' representing wealth related to morality, spiritual upliftment, and charitable endowments.

items.name: **Nila**
items.description: The ''Sapphire'' giving massive resources related to trade, commerce, and material exchange.

items.name: **Kharva**
items.description: The ''Dwarf'' representing wealth intertwined with mixed (both auspicious and complex) desires.

description: In the 29th Chaupai, Tulsidas proclaims that Hanuman's glory is famous across all four ages (*Yugas*). According to Vedic cosmology, time is cyclical, divided into four grand planetary epochs.

items.name: **Satya Yuga**
items.description: The Age of Truth and absolute Purity. Humanity is deeply spiritual, peaceful, and perfectly completely aligned with Dharma.

items.name: **Treta Yuga**
items.description: The Silver Age. Dharma slightly declines. This is the era in which Lord Rama and Hanuman incarnated to establish righteousness.

items.name: **Dvapara Yuga**
items.description: The Bronze Age. Morality drops to 50\%. This era featured the Mahabharata war and the incarnation of Lord Krishna.

items.name: **Kali Yuga**
items.description: The Iron Age (our current era). An age of deep ignorance, conflict, and spiritual amnesia. Hanuman remains immortal (*Chiranjeevi*) physically present on Earth specifically to guide seekers through this dark age.

description: In the very first opening Doha, Tulsidas prays for the ''four fruits'' (*Phala Chaari*). In Vedic philosophy, these are the *Purusharthas*—the four fundamental grand goals or aims of human life that lead to complete fulfillment.

items.name: **Dharma**
items.description: Righteousness, moral duty, and living in cosmic law and harmony. The foundational aim of a noble life.

items.name: **Artha**
items.description: Material prosperity, wealth, economic security, and physical well-being required to sustain life and family.

items.name: **Kama**
items.description: Desire, pleasure, emotional fulfillment, aesthetics, and the enjoyment of the world in a balanced way.

items.name: **Moksha**
items.description: The ultimate liberation. Freedom from the cycle of birth and death (*Samsara*) and union with the divine.
